tholsel_clerk.text: Welcome to the Tholsel. The name comes from 'toll' and an old word for hall. So it is, literally, the Toll Hall.
The building you see went up around 1761, with arches over the pavement and a clock tower on top.
People walk through its arches every day without looking up. Do look up.

then.text: Brennan, Tholsel. I stamp the permits. The Tholsel is where Kilkenny used to collect its tolls, so I am keeping up a fine tradition of bureaucracy.

Permits? Only one this month for anything large: the soup tent at the hurling. Applicant, the Butter Slip Cafe. A 60-litre pot, 'to be sourced'. I underlined it, because I wanted to see who'd source it.

else.text: Lovely old building, this. Ask me again if you ever hear there's trouble.
